title: Another way through (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The walk-in cave is the hall's main encounter: passages that divide and rejoin, a crossing that passes over, a place found again another way. The small grower near the arrival is its other half: the same kind of network at a size that can only be seen.
hero.staging: The cave stood out over the void with nothing leading to it and the grower stood eleven metres east of the arrival; the pass brought the grower to the arrival, declared the cave's floor ground, and built a footbridge into its near mouth and a gangway from its far mouth back round its east side (c52bc2bca). The cave itself is not moved.

plates.title: 1  ENTER, OR ONLY SEE?
front: The hall asks which connections a body can enter, and which it can only see.
On the grower's ring a point reaches for points already there. I can see every link at once.
I cannot walk one of them.
A network drawn at the size of a table is all seeing and no entering.
Most of the networks I describe, I have only ever seen.
back: from here the cave is the dark shape past the north edge. until this pass it was only that.

plates.title: 2  IT CANNOT REACH INTO ITS OWN FUTURE
front: A new point appears and reaches towards points already there.
An older point can receive a relation it could not have anticipated. The newcomer cannot reach into its own future.
There is no declared root. But proximity and time still make some points more available than others.
Nobody chose the old points to be central. They were early.
Arriving first is a position nobody had to defend.
back: a degree is something we can count. influence would need another question. the hall.

plates.title: 3  ONE LINK, OR THREE
front: Hold the growth and compare one link with three. The positions stay. Some of the ways between them disappear.
One link per arrival leaves two separate trees. Three: the first newcomer joins both starting points, and later arrivals make circuits.
No point changed its address. Moving through the network would be a different undertaking.
The number of links changes whether another way through is available.
A map of where things are says nothing about how many ways there are between them.
back: remove a busy point and ask which relations survive. the model can restore it. inventing a new connection would be another act.

plates.title: 4  ITS TERRITORY WAS ALREADY GIVEN
front: The ring does not spread with the shoots.
The machine keeps finding new places inside a boundary it chose before the network began.
Something is growing, but its territory has already been given.
Being well connected here does not tell us who could change the rule that makes these connections.
Growth inside a fixed ring looks like freedom from inside the ring.
back: inside the cave the equivalent will be a wall. we can enjoy what these rules make possible and still want to change where they stop.

plates.title: 5  FROM OUTSIDE, WITH MY EYES
front: From outside, the hall says, you can follow several passages with your eyes. One rises across another.
Two paths seem to intersect. Inside, one passes over the other. You cannot turn at that crossing.
Nearness is not yet a relation you can enter.
On a drawing the two would share a point. In the cave they share nothing but my line of sight.
A crossing I can see is a fact about where I am standing.
back: the gangway down the cave's east side is there for this plate: walk it and look.

plates.title: 6  THERE WAS NO WAY IN
front: The cave stands out over the void. Its near mouth is seven metres past the edge of this floor.
As I found it, nothing led there. The whole encounter the hall describes was a thing to look at.
So: eight metres of planks, joints staggered, into the near mouth. The tower's walker crossed and stood on the cave's floor.
The hall's own question had been answered by the placement: only see.
A connection described in the text and missing on the floor is the commonest kind I make.
back: it took one setting as well as the planks: the cave's floor had to be declared ground.

plates.title: 7  A PLACE BEFORE ITS POSITION
front: Inside, the wall takes away the view. The passage divides. A coloured light gathers at a junction.
You can leave a place and find it again without walking back along the way you came.
The return is possible because the connections contain a circuit. A tree would make me retrace.
A place can become familiar before I can draw its position in the whole.
I knew the violet junction twice before I knew where it was.
back: the walker went mouth to mouth by five of the cave's own places, on the ground passages. it never saw the whole.

plates.title: 8  NEAR IS NOT YET A WAY
front: From the cave's far mouth a gangway comes round the outside and down its east side.
It stops 1.7 m from this wing. From here I can see it. I cannot enter it.
With the panel up there is one way between the floor and the cave. Every visit ends by retracing.
Lay the panel, from either side: two ways. Out is no longer the same as in.
One added connection can change what a journey is. This one is two metres of timber.
back: the walker came round the outside, stood 2 m from the floor's edge with no way on, and laid it.

plates.title: 9  WHERE WOULD YOU PUT ONE?
front: The hall: we can enter its relations and choose among them; we cannot yet make a new opening in its wall.
That is a desire the encounter can produce. Where would you put one? Which two places would become neighbours?
I could not cut the cave. I could add outside it.
The panel is the one connection on this floor a visitor makes. The plates that lay it were put there by me.
Even the freedom to connect arrives through somebody's opening.
back: there is pleasure in finding another way. there can also be shelter in the turn that takes you out of sight.

8 m of planks: a way in

threads.why: A network that can only be seen: watch how one point arrives in it.
A newcomer reaches back; how many links it may make decides the ways.
The number of links is one rule; the ring it grows inside is another.
Enter or only see: as placed, the cave could only be seen.
A footbridge; and inside, the view is taken away.
A place known from inside, then followed with the eyes from the gangway.
Two passages that only seem to meet; a gangway that only seems to arrive.
One added panel changes the journey; who is allowed to add it?
A territory given in advance, and the wish to change where the rules stop.

visual_arguments.title: THE WAY ROUND
visual_arguments.claim: A connection that can be seen is not yet one a body can enter; one added link turns a visit that must retrace itself into a circuit; and who may add the link is a question about the rule, not about the network.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'Which connections can a body enter, and which can it only see?' ... 'From outside, you can follow several passages with your eyes.' ... 'Nearness is not yet a relation you can enter.' ... 'One added connection can change what a journey is.'
built_from: six rows of 4 m and 2 m timber planks with staggered joints: a footbridge eight metres long
plank rails on two-metre plank uprights
twenty-seven timber panels: a gangway 53 m long round the cave
one more panel that plates lay and lift
two plates: one on the floor, one on the gangway
visual_arguments.what_stands: At the middle of the floor's north edge a plank bridge with rails goes out into the mouth of a dark tube; to the east a railed gangway comes down beside the tube and stops short of the east wing.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Cross the footbridge and walk in. Find the far mouth. Come back round the outside on the gangway, looking at the passages you were in. At its end, stand on the plate. Walk onto the wing.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: A cave that is entered where before it was seen; from the gangway, one passage climbing over another; a gap of open air between a gangway and a floor; a panel that closes it.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/way_round_walk.gd, the tower's walker: across the footbridge to stand in the near mouth; through the cave's ground passages by five of its places to the far mouth; the upper passage counted as floor 208; round the outside to the gangway's end, 2 m from the edge and no way on; the panel laid from the gangway and walked over; lifted from the floor (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: The cave still 'leaves the structural floor' for the validator: it does. The pass did not move it onto the slab; it built to it.
Plate 9: the panel is the only connection a visitor makes here, and its plates were placed by the pass. The hall's wish for a new opening in the cave's wall is not granted.
The gangway is 53 m of railed walk over the void. In a headset that may be a great deal; it has rails on both sides and was not tried.
The walker used the cave's ground passages only; the upper route that climbs over was not walked by the probe.
The film monitor beside the grower is not mentioned in the hall text and carries no plate.

board.title: The ways: what the hall says, and what I made of it
board.note: An argument's stickers hung in depth: the hall text's own lines near the cork, the reader's lines in front, tied by red thread (commons/data/arguments/SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network.json).

threads.why: Enter or only see: as the cave was placed, the answer was only see.
A network at the size of a table can be seen whole and entered nowhere.
The newcomer cannot reach forward; the old points are central because they were early.
No declared root: but time makes some points more available.
The positions stay and the ways go: a map of places is not a count of ways.
The number of links decides whether out can differ from in.
Growth in a territory given beforehand looks like freedom from inside it.
Who could change the rule: the plates that lay the panel were placed by someone.
A place familiar before it can be drawn: the violet junction, known twice.
Nearness is not a relation: a crossing seen is a fact about the viewer.
One added connection: a panel, and out is no longer in.
No new opening in the wall; the one that could be made is outside it.
